summary: East-west route detour after enabling regional-locality: EU->APAC TLS/TCP handshake spikes p95
description:
Issue summary: Customer FinStrata reports intermittent increases in p95 latency for requests originating in eu-west after they flipped a regional-locality toggle on their tenant (dedicated). Symptoms began ~2026-03-04 09:00 UTC and are reproducible across multiple sessions.

Impact: Customer observes sustained p95 increase from ~120ms to ~440ms for text-generation calls. End-users in EU see degraded interactivity for document summarization workflows. No 5xx errors reported.

Environment: prod (eu-west tenant, dedicated pool). Model traffic primarily gpt-redwood-1-xl and gpt-redwood-1-large.

Observed behavior: Traces show a subset (~12%) of requests that should stay in eu-west are routed via an APAC edge for the initial TLS/TCP handshake, then proxied back to eu-west serving runtime. This adds ~250–350ms extra latency (DNS+TLS+cross-region RTT). Connection-level logs show repeated TLS renegotiation timestamps aligning with residency-lock refresh window.

Expected behavior: Regional-locality flip should keep traffic within eu-west; if routing fallback occurs it should prefer eu-west fallback pool. No cross-region hairpinning expected for steady-state traffic.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer enabled regional-locality=true for tenant FIN-ACCT-09 at 2026-03-04T08:55 UTC.
2) Run 200 concurrent short-generation requests (seq len 64) from eu-west test clients.
3) Observe p50/p95 on Console and trace sampling.

Logs / snippets (sanitized):
- EDGE-2026-03-04T09:03:14Z connection accepted from 3.76.12.55 (eu-west) -> proxy-ep-01 (apac)
- PROXY-2026-03-04T09:03:15Z upstream connect to eu-west-serving-03 TLS handshake start
- TRACE-ID ab12cd: initial edge hop apac->eu-west added 312ms RTT

Initial hypothesis: Control-plane residency propagation race + DNS rebind caused a small window where token-affinity map pointed to APAC edge despite tenant locality being EU. Another contributor may be TLS session reuse disabled at edge during the lock flip, triggering full handshake via wrong egress.

Immediate mitigation attempted: Support requested customer to toggle regional-locality back off; traffic returned to normal within ~7 minutes. We also rolled a targeted edge route cache flush for tenant token on eu-west edges.

Investigation plan:
- Validate control-plane event timeline and token-affinity entries at the time of the flip.
- Correlate edge DNS cache TTLs and healthcheck timestamps for eu-west vs apac edges.
- Check scheduler/placement logs for any recent GPU rebalances that might have flipped preferred fallback priority.
- Reproduce in staging with a staged residency flip while capturing full tcpdump on edge and serving nodes.

Customer request: A formal explanation of why a portion of traffic briefly egressed to APAC and confirmation that enabling regional-locality will not cause repeat cross-region hairpins. They also asked for longer-term guardrail (control-plane sequencing / token lockatomicity) and request a postmortem if production regression.
